newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DE BEERS SHARES FALL ON HIGHER TAX RATE.
newsitem.headline: DE BEERS SHARES FALL ON HIGHER TAX RATE.

text.p: Shares in De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd slipped on Tuesday knocked by a higher rate of taxation in the half-year ended June 30, analysts said.
Tax payable by De Beers and its international arm De Beers Centenary AG was $156 million in the interim period compared to $105 million in the same period last year.
"The bottom line earnings may not be as high as expected, but principally because of a higher rate of tax," Des Mayers, diamond analyst at O'Flaherty, Sundelson & Co told Reuters.
The share fell 300 cents to 168 rand after the results with turnover at 31 million rand. It traded as high as 171.75 rand in anticipation of the results in the morning.
Analysts said it was dificult to issue a full analysis of the results because little information was released with the results.
"There is no more information that is available yet. They have only put out certain of the figures only at this stage and that makes life very difficult," Mayers said.
The growth in the diamond account profitability up about 14 percent to $510 million was lauded by analysts.
De Beers and De Beers Centenary reported combined earnings per linked unit rising to 204 U.S. cents in the interim period from 180 U.S. cents in the same period last year.
